Acceptance criteria coverage - **Core Functionality (specific, actionable messages)** - All six primary validation rules implement meta.messages with specific templates and placeholders ({{name}}, {{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{path}}, {{reqId}}, {{storyPath}}, {{error}}). - Tests across rule suites verify both valid and invalid cases, ensuring no generic fallback messages are used for these violations.
- **Quality Standards (ESLint best practices)** - All messages are implemented via meta.messages and referenced by messageId in context.report, following ESLint recommendations. - Error-reporting tests verify proper use of messageId/data and suggestion API for require-story-annotation; other rules similarly use context.report with data placeholders.
- **Integration with ESLint reporting** - All reporting uses context.report with node references and messageId/data. - For missing annotations, location is targeted at function identifiers or branch nodes (e.g., getNameNodeForReqReport, branch node context). - Jest run (39 suites, 299 tests, 0 failures) confirms end-to-end integration for these rules within Jest RuleTester and custom contexts.
- **User Experience (problem, location, suggested fix)** - Problem: Each rule’s message explains exactly what is missing/invalid. - Location: Function/method name in messages; node locations provided via AST nodes; utilities explicitly choose precise nodes (identifiers) where possible. - Suggested fix: require-story-annotation and branch-annotation helpers offer ESLint autofixes; error-reporting.test.ts asserts suggestion descriptions and fix functions. valid-annotation-format implements safe auto-fixes for path suffixes.
- **Error Handling (incomplete context / I/O issues)** - storyReferenceUtils and valid-story-reference distinguish missing vs fs-error, never throw, and surface details via {{error}}. - valid-annotation-format handles invalid regex configs via invalidRuleConfiguration and continues validation with defaults. - valid-req-reference caches reads and treats failures as empty sets instead of crashing. - annotation-checker and other helpers fall back to safe defaults like "(anonymous)" when names are not available.
- **Documentation / Conventions** - The story itself documents conventions, and code comments/JSDoc tags directly reference docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and its REQ-* IDs across the core rules and helpers (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference, annotation-checker, storyReferenceUtils). - Error message patterns in the code match the patterns described in the story (function-related, branch-related, format details, file/reference, severity mapping).

traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md describes cross-cutting error reporting behavior for all core traceability validation rules. The implementation provides: - Specific, contextual error messages for each rule via meta.messages and structured placeholders. - Precise location reporting using identifier and branch nodes. - Actionable suggestions, including ESLint suggestions and autofixes where appropriate. - Consistent error patterns for functions, branches, formats, and file/requirement references. - Severity mapping that treats missing annotations and unresolved references as errors and format issues as warnings, implemented in the plugin configs and verified by tests. - Robust error handling for filesystem and configuration edge cases.
Dedicated tests in tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts explicitly support this story and verify REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, and REQ-ERROR-LOCATION for require-story-annotation. Other rule and config tests cover severity and conventions across the wider ruleset. All tests currently pass, and the codebase is extensively annotated with @story/@req/@supports references back to this story. Therefore, all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are implemented and verified.
